**Construction.** Let $\varepsilon_k(n)\in\{0,1\}$ be the $k$-th binary digit of $n$, so $n=\sum_{k\ge0}\varepsilon_k(n)2^k$. Define

$$x_n=K\sum_{k\ge 0}\varepsilon_k(n)\,2^{-ak},\qquad K=\frac{2^a-1}{2^a-2}.$$

This is well defined since $a>1$ makes $2^a>2$, so $K$ is finite and positive.

**Boundedness.** $|x_n|\le K\sum_{k\ge0}2^{-ak}=\dfrac{K}{1-2^{-a}}=:C$ for all $n$.

**Separation.** Let $i\ne j$, and let $m$ be the smallest index with $\varepsilon_m(i)\ne\varepsilon_m(j)$. Then $i\equiv j \pmod{2^m}$ and $i\ne j$, so $|i-j|\ge 2^m$. Hence
$$|i-j|^{-a}\le 2^{-am}.$$

Write $e_k=\varepsilon_k(i)-\varepsilon_k(j)$. Then $e_k=0$ for $k<m$, $|e_m|=1$, and $|e_k|\le 1$ for all $k$. So
$$\frac{x_i-x_j}{K}=e_m2^{-am}+\sum_{k>m}e_k2^{-ak},$$
and
$$\Big|\sum_{k>m}e_k2^{-ak}\Big|\le\sum_{k>m}2^{-ak}=\frac{2^{-am}}{2^a-1}.$$
Therefore
$$|x_i-x_j|\ge K\,2^{-am}\Big(1-\frac{1}{2^a-1}\Big)=K\,2^{-am}\cdot\frac{2^a-2}{2^a-1}=2^{-am}.$$

Combining the two bounds,
$$|x_i-x_j|\ge 2^{-am}\ge |i-j|^{-a},$$
so $|x_i-x_j|\,|i-j|^{a}\ge 1$ for all distinct nonnegative integers $i,j$.

ANSWER: $x_n=\dfrac{2^a-1}{2^a-2}\displaystyle\sum_{k\ge0}\varepsilon_k(n)\,2^{-ak}$, where $\varepsilon_k(n)$ is the $k$-th binary digit of $n$.
